questions.problem:
To prepare liquid fertilizer, $5.5$ grams of fertilizer powder should be dissolved in a liter of water. How much powder must be dissolved in $8.6$ liters of water to make fertilizer?

Expressed as a decimal, 
{{field-1}}
$\,$grams of powder must be dissolved in $8.6$ liters of water.
questions.worked_solution:
To determine the amount of powder that must be dissolved in $8.6$ liters of water, we have to multiply $8.6$ by $5.5.$

We proceed by multiplying the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{3} \\ \boxed{3}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{0}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  &  & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.5\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,7\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in $8.6$ and there is $1$ decimal place in $5.5.$
Therefore, their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

So, we take our value of $4730$ and add a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places.

$$
47\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{30}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Hence, $8.6\times 5.5=47.30=47.3.$

We conclude that $47.3$ grams of powder must be dissolved in $8.6$ liters of water.

questions.problem:
Orlando used $0.3\,\text{kg}$ of powdered fertilizer on Monday morning. He then used $0.18\,\text{kg}$ of powdered fertilizer on Monday afternoon. How much powder did Orlando use that day?

Expressed as a decimal, Orlando used$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\text{kg}$ of powdered fertilizer.
questions.worked_solution:
To determine the amount of powder Orlando used, we need to calculate the sum $0.3+0.18.$

There is $1$ decimal place in $0.3$ and $2$ decimal places in $0.18.$

To add the numbers, they both need to have the same number of decimals. Hence, we rewrite the first number so that it has $2$ decimal places:

$$
0.3=0.30
$$

Next, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we proceed by adding the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ \end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, Orlando used $0.48\,\text{kg}$ of powdered fertilizer.

questions.problem:
During a particular weekend, Orlando made $10\,\frac{1}{2}$ liters of liquid fertilizer. He used $9\,\frac{1}{6}$ liters from this amount. How much liquid fertilizer did Orlando have left over? Express your answer as a mixed number in its lowest terms.

Orlando had$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\,$liters of liquid fertilizer left over.
questions.worked_solution:
Orlando had $(10\,\frac{1}{2}-9\,\frac{1}{6})$ liters of liquid fertilizer left over.

Writing $10\,\frac{1}{2}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
10\,\frac{1}{2}=\frac{10\times 2+1}{2}=\frac{21}{2}.
$$

Writing $9\,\frac{1}{6}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
9\,\frac{1}{6}=\frac{9\times 6+1}{6}=\frac{55}{6}.
$$

Therefore, our problem now is to work out the following:

$$
\frac{21}{2}-\frac{55}{6}
$$

To subtract two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator.

In this question, we can make a common denominator of $6.$

To put $\frac{21}{2}$ over a denominator of $6,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $3:$

$$
\frac{21}{2}=\frac{21\times 3}{2\times 3}=\frac{63}{6}
$$

We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators:

$$
\frac{63}{6}-\frac{55}{6}=\frac{8}{6}
$$

Simplifying, we have

$$
\frac{8}{6}=\frac{8÷2}{6÷2}=\frac{4}{3}.
$$

Finally, we convert back to a mixed number:

$$
\frac{4}{3}=1\,\text{R}\,1=1\,\frac{1}{3}
$$

Therefore, Orlando had $1\,\frac{1}{3}$ liters of liquid fertilizer left over.

questions.problem:
Orlando bought $6$ packages of powdered fertilizer, for which he paid $$96.44.$ Estimate the price of each package by rounding the amount of money he spent to the nearest dollar.

The approximate price of each package is $
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To estimate the price of each package, we need to find an approximation to $96.44÷6.$

So, we round the dividend to the nearest whole number:

$$
96.44\to 96
$$

Now, we divide $96$ by $6$ as usual:

$$
96÷6=16
$$

Therefore, the approximate price of each package is $$16.$
